newsitem.title: UK: British court jails third Kray brother.
newsitem.headline: British court jails third Kray brother.

text.p: The elder brother of former British gangland twins Reggie and Ronnie Kray, who terrorised London in the 1960s, was jailed on Monday for 12 years for masterminding a 39 million pound ($65 million) cocaine plot.
Charlie Kray, a 70-year-old former boxer, protested his innocence as he was led from the courtroom at Woolwich, east London.
"All my life I have advised people never to be involved in drugs," he said.
However the jury, which on Friday convicted Kray of supplying and offering to supply cocaine, was clearly of the opinion that he had failed to follow his own advice.
Judge Michael Carroll told him: "You showed yourself to be ready, willing and able to lend yourself to any criminal enterprise which became known to you."
Kray was convicted of offering to supply two undercover police officers with five kg (11 lb) of cocaine every fortnight for two years. He was also found guilty of actually supplying two kg (4.4 lb).
The defence portrayed Kray as a poor and sick old man who had pretended to have access to drugs to try to make some money out of the officers.
During the trial, the jury heard evidence from former gangland leader "Mad" Frankie Fraser and other character witnesses who insisted Kray was "too nice" to break the law.
His brothers Reggie and Ronnie, London's most prominent gang bosses during the 1960s, were jailed for life in 1969 for the murders of fellow criminals George Cornell and Jack "The Hat" McVitie.
Charlie Kray was always the quiet one, but he was jailed for 10 years for helping to dispose of McVitie's body.
Ronnie died of a heart attack last year in Broadmoor psychiatric hospital, home to many of Britain's most disturbed criminals. Reggie, 62, remains in prison.

The Kray twins' thuggery has become romanticised over the years they have been in prison. A film was made of their lives, and their defenders argue that their reign helped to keep the peace in the impoverished East End of London. They say the brothers only ever attacked other villains.
Charlie Kray's friends and relatives have said he will appeal against his conviction.
